learningObjective: Diagnose a TorchDynamo graph break caused by a Python-object side effect and describe the resulting graph-split behavior.

canonicalClaims.claim: TorchDynamo produces a graph break when it encounters Python bytecode whose faithful tracing would require modeling arbitrary side effects on non-tensor objects; it splits the compiled function around the offending bytecode and runs that step in eager Python.
conditions: The mutated object is a user-defined Python class, not a specially-handled type (tensor, nn.Module, etc.).
nonImplications: Does not imply that the surrounding compiled subgraphs are invalidated; they still run compiled.
Does not imply that removing the print/attribute-set fixes performance in every case; graph-break cost depends on frequency.

sourceMappings.locator: TorchDynamo overview — supported Python semantics and graph breaks
PyTorch 2 ASPLOS 2024 — bytecode transformation and side effects

misconceptions.claim: `+=` on a Python integer attribute triggers a graph break because the operator itself is unsupported; rewriting as `x = x + 1` avoids it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `+=` desugars to LOAD_ATTR / BINARY_ADD / STORE_ATTR; STORE_ATTR on a non-tensor Python object is the root cause, and the manual rewrite emits the same bytecode.

misconceptions.claim: `fullgraph=False` disables all graph breaks; the log must be from a stale build.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `fullgraph=False` permits graph breaks (defaults to allowing them); `fullgraph=True` raises when a break would occur.

misconceptions.claim: Graph breaks only occur for data-dependent control flow on tensors; Python side effects never cause them.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Python side effects (list.append on external lists, prints, attribute mutation) are a well-known category of graph-break triggers.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: TorchDynamo docs — 'Common causes of graph breaks'

misconceptions.claim: `torch.relu` is not supported under `fullgraph=False`; the graph break originates from that op.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `torch.relu` is a first-class supported op; the graph break location is dictated by the STORE_ATTR bytecode.

implementationFacts: TorchDynamo captures Python bytecode; graph breaks split the frame at the offending bytecode
`fullgraph=True` converts what would be a graph break into an error
Common graph-break triggers: Python side effects, data-dependent control flow, unsupported ops, custom operators without meta implementations
performanceScenarios: Frequent graph breaks per iteration inflate CPU-side dispatch cost and prevent long fused kernels; identifying and removing them is a common torch.compile tuning task.
